Partially answerable from the context.

**Trailing `\r` printed?** In `visibleLineEnd`, the visible line end is found at the next `\n` (or end of data). With `crlf` set, if the line is non-empty and the byte before `\n` is `\r`, the end is moved back by one so the `\r` is excluded from the visible line (src/scan.zig:246-247). That suggests the `\r` isn't part of the visible text, but the context doesn't show the printing code, so I can't confirm that nothing else prints it.

**One terminator or two?** The function treats `\r\n` as a single terminator: it finds only `\n` and strips an adjacent `\r` (src/scan.zig:246-247). It doesn't treat `\r` alone as a terminator. Whether line counting elsewhere agrees isn't shown.

**Missing:** the callers of `visibleLineEnd`, the output and printing code, and any line-counting code.
